subject.title: [Feature]: Add tools.web.fetch.allowPrivateNetwork to allow private network access

question: Should OpenClaw expose private-network access for arbitrary web_fetch URLs, and should the permanent contract be global, per-agent, host-scoped, confirmation-based, or combined with metadata/link-local/redirect/audit constraints?
rationale: The request changes the SSRF boundary for a model-callable network tool and adds security-sensitive configuration surface, so repository policy requires maintainer product/security intent before implementation.

options.title: Sponsor Scoped Per-Agent Policy
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/67421 or a successor to expose private-network access only through explicit scoped policy with cache, redirect, metadata, docs, and audit safeguards.

options.title: Keep Arbitrary web_fetch Strict
options.body: Reject broad private-network access for arbitrary `web_fetch` and document supported alternatives such as fake-IP proxy opt-ins, trusted proxy mode, hostname allowlists, or browser/tool-specific controls.

options.title: Accept A Simpler Global Flag
options.body: Expose a global dangerous flag for trusted deployments, accepting a wider blast radius and requiring strong docs, tests, and security audit coverage before merge.

recommendation.title: Sponsor Scoped Per-Agent Policy
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/67421 or a successor to expose private-network access only through explicit scoped policy with cache, redirect, metadata, docs, and audit safeguards.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest history on the central SSRF/web_fetch policy path and already stated the remaining maintainer decision in the issue discussion.
